subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared filename decoder live, and should the existing candidate PR be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects core media, bundled channel plugins, and plugin-facing reuse; automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use media-core/plugin-safe decoder
options.body: Move the decoder into the media-core or explicitly exported plugin-safe boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that one shared helper.

options.title: Keep Feishu-only repairs
options.body: Treat current Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and leave non-Feishu multi-encoding cases to future reports, accepting continued parser drift.

options.title: Pause until broader repros arrive
options.body: Keep the issue open but require concrete non-Feishu channel failures before approving shared utility work.

recommendation.title: Use media-core/plugin-safe decoder
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into the media-core or explicitly exported plugin-safe boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that one shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Feishu filename recovery and media-core release work make this the strongest available owner for the API-boundary choice.
